mechanical.notes: 11/11 suites after the fix. Console clean across 4 re-captured states. THE DISCOVERY (from holding the psu-state-colours finding): chassis_body was a SOLID BOX up to the front plane, so the entire front was BURIED inside it — 9 module faces, 3 PSU faces, 13 LEDs, RJ45 cage/throat, every divider and cavity. A camera ray hit chassis_body first in every view; the only things rendering for three passes were the 4 pieces that PROTRUDE (module+PSU handles, alarm block, livery), which read convincingly enough as 'a row of bays' to pass blockout/structural/materials. WHY NO GUARD SAW IT: verifyBaysAreRecessed measured DEPTH BEHIND THE FRONT PLANE — which is exactly what a buried piece does; WITHOUT AN OPENING, RECESSED IS BURIED, and the guard never asked whether a hole existed. Everything else was satisfied (in-envelope, attached to the box they were inside, right size/colour, counted, complete). BEING INVISIBLE was not a property anything measured. FIX: the shell ends 12.5 mm behind the front and the face is a FRAME (four bars leaving the aperture open); the cavity moved behind the face. New guard verifyBayContentsAreVisible: every module/PSU/NMC face, LED and cage must be reachable by a front-axis ray, SAMPLED per-face (a piece can be legitimately covered at one point by something mounted ON it — the RJ45 cage sits mid-face); negative control: re-closing the aperture reports 27 hidden, 0 as-built. A second self-introduced defect (dividers + blanks hanging off the moved cavity, 3.6 mm behind) was caught by verifyNothingFloats (0 in all, 3 in partial) and fixed. AND my question exposed a blind spot in his own metric: irradiance() returned a LUMA and the materials check multiplied each colour channel by that scalar, modelling the rig as WHITE (it is not: b/r = 1.069) — corrected to PER-CHANNEL irradiance with the lamp assertion on the rendered pixel. Verified: 0 bay pieces blocked from the front (27 when closed), lamps green-dominant/blue-dominant per-channel, 0 floating in both module states, panel exposures unchanged, camera P2 prediction still exact.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. This pass is the one that made the asset REAL: holding the psu-state-colours finding (green not reading) instead of passing it uncovered that chassis_body was a solid box burying the ENTIRE front — nine faces, three PSU faces, thirteen LEDs, cage, dividers, cavities — with only four protruding pieces rendering for three prior gates, mine included. My specific pixel values were mis-attributed to the DOM (the pass captures --page), but the zero-green signal was real and pointed at a far worse defect than a lamp; had I rubber-stamped it, it reaches P6. The lesson is sharp and general: WITHOUT AN OPENING, RECESSED IS BURIED — a depth-behind-the-plane guard cannot see an invisible part, so visibility must be asserted with a ray that reaches the piece. The fix (framed face + open aperture + per-face visibility guard with a negative control) is verified, and the per-channel irradiance correction now judges lamp hue on the rendered pixel. The front finally renders, all criticals read, and the PSU state hue reads blue->green. Cleared to the optimization pass.
